title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
description: Code, data and results for the paper. Offline retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on edge devices is updated through signed knowledge packs that carry text and precomputed embedding vectors. A signature proves who published a pack, not that its vectors encode its text. The paper measures this text-vector integrity gap: a verifier that accepts vectors within a cosine tolerance concedes a share of queries given by the distribution of angular retrieval margins (the margin law); tolerance-based audits of compressed vector stores leave up to all queries exposed, as an executed attack on a FAISS product-quantisation index shows; and code-level verification with verifier-decided ambiguity and canonicalisation closes the gap. The repository contains the reference verifier, the experiment and analysis scripts, the SQuAD-derived data, all per-query results and the protocol. Code and our results: MIT; SQuAD-derived data, vectors and results containing SQuAD text: CC BY-SA 4.0; answers generated with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct are also subject to the Qwen Research License Agreement; for the BEIR corpora and MS MARCO only derived numbers and identifiers are included (see DATA_LICENSES.md).
